prompt: The September Declaration has a rough equivalent in the Netherlands that takes place on the same day every year. In what century was the current name of this day (as of August 2024) chosen?
answer: The Dutch equivalent is **Prinsjesdag**, held on the **third Tuesday of September**. Its name dates from the **18th century**, when “Prinsjesdag” referred to the birthday of Prince William V. It was later applied to the parliamentary opening ceremony, beginning in the 19th century.
